evidence: paper: \partial_\theta f = 0, \qquad \forall I \in \mathbb{N}_0^5\ \exists C_{j,I}, b_{j,I}, d_{j,I} :\ |\partial^I f| \le C_{j,I}\,\varepsilon^{\alpha} S_*^{\,b_{j,I}}\,\zeta\,\delta^{-d_{j,I}} .

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Unfolding MeanClass gives, for every finite order m, a single pair (C, p) with ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ j f x‖ ≤ C · ε^α · (S_* · max{1, δ(x)⁻¹})^p · ζ(x) for all j ≤ m and all x in the strip domain. Three encoding differences, all routine: (i) derivatives are iterated Fréchet jets of order j rather than coordinate multi-indices ∂^I (see eq-p069-4); (ii) the paper's constants C_{j,I}, b_{j,I}, d_{j,I} depend on the individual multi-index, the Lean's on the order bound m only — the two are interchangeable because for each m there are finitely many I with |I| ≤ m, so one takes the maximum of the C's and of the b's and d's; the Lean also couples the S_* and δ exponents into one exponent p, which is harmless upward since S_* ≥ 1 (StripData.one_le_slow) and max{1, δ⁻¹} ≥ 1, so (S_* · max{1,δ⁻¹})^p ≥ max over b,d ≤ p of S_*^b δ^{-d}; (iii) `max 1 (s.delta x)⁻¹` equals δ(x)⁻¹ exactly on the paper's weight because (6.23) sets δ = min{1, …} ≤ 1, so δ⁻¹ ≥ 1, and the Lean's exponent p is a natural number where the paper's d_{j,I} is unconstrained — rounding d up to an integer only weakens the bound, in the direction the class needs. The clause ∂_θ f = 0 is not a field of MeanClass: axisymmetry is encoded structurally, by the chart carrying no θ coordinate at all — the instantiation BaseContextAssembly.nativeStrip is a StripData over LocalSignedRequest.Point = PressureStream.Lift Plane = ℝ × ((ℝ×ℝ) × (ℝ×ℝ)) (PressureStream.lean:25–26), five real coordinates and no angular one, and the paper's own display is for f = f(R,Z,T,H) — so every function in the class is θ-independent by construction rather than by hypothesis. That reading is attributed to the chart, not to the atlas: the atlas does not corroborate it but says the opposite in emphasis, recording at /home/jack/ns-audit-data/atlas.md:4225 that MeanClass "Encodes only the bound (6.24)" and "omits torus descent (6.20), ∂_θ f = 0, and the shell support/zero-extension conditions".
